steps.title: Module boss
steps.body: These combine lists, dicts, sets, comprehensions, `sorted(key=...)` and `collections`. Plan the data structure first: most of the work disappears when you pick the right one.

steps.title: Anagram groups
prompt: Read one line of words. Group words that are anagrams of each other (same letters, ignoring case). Print each group that has **more than one** word, as the words in their original order separated by spaces, groups ordered by the first appearance of their first word. If there are none, print `no anagrams`.
`listen post silent stop pots enlist cat` gives:
solution: found = [g for g in groups.values() if len(g) > 1]

tests.name: two groups
tests.stdin: listen post silent stop pots enlist cat

hints: Sorting the letters gives the same key for all anagrams: `"".join(sorted(w.lower()))`.
`defaultdict(list)` keeps insertion order, so groups come out in first-appearance order.

steps.title: Matrix transpose
prompt: Read lines of space-separated numbers until a blank line. They form a rectangular matrix. Print its transpose (rows become columns), each row space-separated.
hints: `while line := input():` stops on the blank line because `""` is falsy.
`zip(*rows)` passes each row as a separate argument, pairing up the first items, the second items, and so on.

steps.title: Inventory report
prompt: Read lines of `category item quantity` until `end`. Print, for each category in alphabetical order, the category, its total quantity, and its items sorted by quantity (highest first, then by name), in this format:
If the same item appears twice in a category, add the quantities. Then print `low stock: ...` listing (alphabetically) every item with quantity under 3, or `low stock: none`.
solution: listing = ", ".join(f"{name} {q}" for name, q in items)
low = sorted(name for c in stock.values() for name, q in c.items() if q < 3)

tests.name: example
tests.stdin:
fruit apple 5
veg leek 4
fruit pear 3
fruit kiwi 2
fruit apple 2
end

hints: A `defaultdict(Counter)` maps each category to its own counter.
A comprehension with two `for`s can collect the low-stock names across all categories.
